scope: Course-level supplement chapter grounded in official Stanford course-site pages only.
strengths: The supplement stays explicitly grounded in the official Stanford course page and official schedule only.
It clearly distinguishes canonical sources from the instructor-affiliated but non-canonical public playlist.
It explains how CS329A extends the Berkeley Spring 2025 textbook on self-improvement, verifier-centered learning, planning, coding agents, evaluation, research automation, memory, and robotics.
It records source gaps honestly instead of pretending to have lecture media.

non_blocking_issues.problem: No official public video page or official slide page was found on the Stanford course site.
non_blocking_issues.impact: The supplement can only be schedule-and-readings-based, not a full lecture reconstruction.

non_blocking_issues.problem: Several guest lectures expose only topic titles and no official reading list.
non_blocking_issues.impact: Those sessions are covered as curricular signals and integration points rather than full technical lecture reconstructions.

non_blocking_issues.problem: The standalone supplement TeX compiles, but the build emits non-blocking Overfull/Underfull box warnings in some bilingual headings and table cells.
non_blocking_issues.impact: The PDF is readable and usable, but a later polish pass could improve line breaking.

residual_risks: If Stanford later publishes official recordings or slide decks, this supplement should be revised and expanded.
Because paper internals were not reconstructed from non-official sources, some sections remain intentionally thematic rather than method-by-method.
decision_rationale: Overall pass is justified because the chapter is solid within its true evidence boundary: it is detailed, textbook-like, explicit about omissions, strongly grounded in official sources, and useful as a supplement to the existing Berkeley Spring 2025 textbook.
